sections.imaging_for_suspected_NSTE-ACS: In patients with suspected ACS, non-elevated (or uncertain) hs-cTn, no ECG changes and no recurrence of pain, incorporate CTCA or a non-invasive stress imaging test as part of the initial workup. In patients with no recurrence of chest pain, normal ECG and normal troponin but still suspected ACS, a non-invasive test (preferably with imaging) for inducible ischemia or CTCA is recommended before deciding on an invasive approach.
sections.timing_of_invasive_strategy_in_NSTE-ACS: An early invasive strategy within 24 h is recommended in patients with high-risk criteria including confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI (per recommended algorithms), dynamic or presumably new contiguous ST/T-segment changes, transient ST-segment elevation, or GRACE risk score >140.
sections.antiplatelet_and_anticoagulant_therapy_i: A potent P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor), or clopidogrel if these are unavailable or contraindicated, is recommended before (or at the time of) PCI and maintained over 12 months unless contraindicated. Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in patients undergoing a primary PCI strategy.
sections.long_term_antithrombotic_therapy: After stent implantation, stopping aspirin after 3–6 months should be considered depending on ischemic vs bleeding risk. In patients event-free after 3–6 months of DAPT and not high ischemic risk, single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT), preferably with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor, should be considered.
sections.cardiac_arrest_and_out_of_hospital_manag: Delayed angiography (vs immediate) may be considered among haemodynamically stable patients without ST-elevation after successful resuscitation from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Targeted temperature management is recommended for patients who remain unconscious after resuscitation.
sections.in_hospital_management: When echocardiography is suboptimal or inconclusive, CMR imaging may be considered.
sections.multivessel_disease_in_STEMI: Routine revascularization of non-IRA lesions should be considered in STEMI patients with multivessel disease before hospital discharge; complete revascularization is recommended either during index PCI or within 45 days.
sections.acute_coronary_syndrome_comorbid_conditi: Glucose-lowering therapy should be considered in ACS patients with persistent hyperglycaemia; avoid episodes of hypoglycaemia.
